$comment: Machine-readable delta registry for hermes-agent. Every change we carry on top of the pinned upstream tag lives here with the reason and the condition under which it can be dropped; hermes-upstream-check.mjs compares it against upstream and flags the deltas upstream has caught up with. Docs: docs/myrmidon/hermes-deltas.md. Keep pinnedRef/pinnedVersion in sync with docker/bot-runtime/Dockerfile (the checker fails when they disagree). `source` stays the upstream repository (that is what the pin is compared against); the image itself clones `docker/bot-runtime/Dockerfile`'s HERMES_REPO, our mirror fork — see the 'Not deltas' section of the docs.

hindsightPlugin.$comment: The memory provider we vendor, recorded here (not read from a file: the hermes catalog entry lives inside the hermes checkout, not in this repository). The image reads plugin-catalog/hindsight.yaml from the pinned hermes tag and fails the build when this pin disagrees; the checker probes the plugin's own default branch.

deltas.reason: The bash session snapshot lives in a shared temp dir and every profile in a container runs as one uid, so credential-shaped env values dumped there were readable by a neighbouring profile.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream excludes credential-shaped env names from the session snapshot by itself.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: publishing to a third-party repository needs the publisher-scan wrapper (plan item PUBLISH-SCAN), which does not exist; the text is prepared in the ticket for the operator to submit.

deltas.reason: Two concurrent runs of one agent (a writer and a session-history reader) made the reader fail with "database is locked": the read path replayed only "disk I/O error".
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream retries a locked read in _read_retrying_ioerr.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: see the note on delta 02 (publisher-scan wrapper pending).

deltas.reason: The stock asyncio default executor is small and a live run holds one worker for its whole life, so the board's POST /v1/runs create calls timed out behind parallel runs.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream sizes the gateway's default executor above the fleet's concurrent runs, or ships an equivalent setting.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: see the note on delta 02 (publisher-scan wrapper pending).

deltas.reason: Before every state-DB write the gateway probes whether the WAL/SHM generation this handle opened is still on disk. When the handle has no recorded sidecar identity the probe readlinks every open descriptor of the process on the calling thread — the gateway's event loop. A state.db reached through a symlink never records an identity (SQLite puts -wal/-shm next to the link target, so the literal <path>-wal never stats), so a multi-profile gateway with hundreds of descriptors walked /proc/self/fd once per write and starved the out-of-loop liveness watchdog into a hard exit (75), failing every run in flight. Same verdict, at most one walk per second per handle.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream stops walking /proc/self/fd on the write path: a cached probe verdict, a minimum interval between probes, or the probe moved off the caller's thread.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: see the note on delta 02 (publisher-scan wrapper pending).

deltas.reason: The run harness removes each run's scratch dir at the run boundary. A path remembered mid-session then succeeds again the moment a write tool's folded mkdir -p re-creates the missing paperclip-run-* parent: mode 755, no run-scratch marker file, never reclaimed — unmarked residue in the shared /tmp holding payloads and comment bodies readable to every co-tenant agent in the container. The guard refuses a write whose ancestor is a removed run-scratch root; a live root and dirs outside the class are untouched, and the guard fails open on its own errors.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream ships an equivalent guard in agent/file_safety.py / tools/file_operations.py: a write into a removed run-scratch root is refused instead of re-creating it.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: see the note on delta 02 (publisher-scan wrapper pending).

deltas.reason: Same change as delta 07: the guard has to run on both write paths the model can reach (write_file, patch_replace) and at the _atomic_write chokepoint where the folded mkdir -p lives, which also covers the V4A patch path. The two patches are one change, split only to keep the diffs file-sized.
deltas.dropCondition: Same as delta 07: upstream refuses a write into a removed run-scratch root on its own write paths.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: see the note on delta 02 (publisher-scan wrapper pending).

deltas.reason: The board mints a run-bound github_credentials capability for container agents, but a hermes gateway has no per-run process to inherit env from, so the capability had no delivery path and container agents could not push. /v1/runs now accepts a github_broker body field and binds it per-run through contextvars; the terminal child-env bridge exports it to that run's subprocesses only.
deltas.dropCondition: Upstream ships a per-run credential-delivery field on /v1/runs with equivalent concurrency isolation.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: see the note on delta 02 (publisher-scan wrapper pending).

deltas.reason: The catalog Hindsight plugin uses one shared client timeout for recall, retain and reflect, and has no way to skip the expensive consolidated-observations layer; a reflect call routinely outlives a recall-sized timeout. The in-tree provider we used to patch had a reflect-specific timeout, a fact-type filter and a bounded retry on the bank's 503 admission refusal.
deltas.dropCondition: The catalog plugin gains a reflect-specific timeout (or a per-operation timeout), a reflect fact-type filter, or the 503 retry.
deltas.offerNote: Not offered yet: the change is small and self-contained but publishing to a third-party repository needs the publisher-scan wrapper (plan item PUBLISH-SCAN) first; the offer text is prepared in the ticket for the operator.
